title: Bass Edwards and the Charlie Johnson band at Small's Paradise
summary: Greer describes Bass Edwards, the sousaphonist with a cigar in his mouth and a light in his bell.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: They would come up to Harlem and hang out all the joints, to steal, see what the cats was putting out. They could play what was on paper, but you couldn't tell them go on out there and play me some choruses. We had a bass player Bass Edwards, he used to record with us a lot. Played one of them big Sousaphones, this cat played with Charlie Johnson

band at Small's Paradise. Charlie Johnson had a good band. (Stafford) Georgie, his drummer, Jabo, and all them sharks in there. This this big. And he had a light in the bell. He'd take the tray and fan Bass Edwards, he took a waiter's tray, like the trumpet player play and play you ten choruses like on the trumpet and he always had cigar, never take it out of his mouth.
That was his trademark. Bass Edwards, boy, he was something else. People come up there to see him. This guy is crazy and you have heard of Bix Beiderbecke?
